name: Terrain Tile Serving Flow
description: WASM-served quantized-mesh terrain (mount /api/v1/terrain/, config-mounted on the sdn-server lane). A $HTQ HttpRequest enters on the http-request trigger; terrain-source:route strips the configured mount PREFIX (config key terrain_mount_path, default the basePath below; a path that does not start with it is a 404, so one tile is reachable at exactly one URL) and takes exactly one of four paths. "" or "catalogue.json" => THE CATALOGUE, the mount's answer to the only question a client cannot answer itself: which tileset epoch to fetch. Owner 2026-08-27 - terrain files are requested over IPFS, so the pyramid is published as one content-addressed directory per epoch (layer.json plus every {z}/{x}/{y}.terrain, the water mask inside each tile) added and pinned through the node's IPFS API by the off-fleet builder, and clients point a native CesiumTerrainProvider at <node>/ipfs/<cid>/. This route names that CID (config key terrain_tileset_cid) with a RELATIVE terrainBasePath a client joins against the node origin it already knows, so no client learns a hostname or hardcodes an epoch; public max-age=60 and a strong ETag, because everything under a CID is immutable and this is the lane's one mutable pointer. With no CID configured it answers delivery "mount" and its own mount path, which is what makes a development node with no IPFS daemon work unchanged. The two routes below are then the same-origin fallback and the local-development path, not the delivery path. "layer.json" => a layer_plan frame for terrain-source:layer_json, which renders the complete tilejson-2.1.0 body (format quantized-mesh-1.0, scheme tms, EPSG:4326, extensions [watermask], availability VERBATIM from the flow config key terrain_available - the availability index is the ingest orchestrator's knowledge and is configured, not aggregated per request at first light) inside the canonical $HTR envelope. "{z}/{x}/{y}.terrain" => a {sql,params} frame for hostcap/flatsql-query:query (SELECT _data FROM DTT WHERE TILESET_ID/LEVEL/X/Y ORDER BY _rowid DESC LIMIT 1 - the newest stored record for the address wins. _rowid, NOT rowid: on a node the relation named DTT is a unified VIEW over per-source shadow tables and a view has no implicit rowid, so the old spelling was 'no such column' on every real node while parsing fine off-node) plus a context frame carrying the address and the client's If-None-Match; terrain-source:respond walks the returned aligned size-prefixed $DTT stream and serves the record's payload with content-type from the record, cache-control public max-age=86400, vary accept-encoding, x-content-type-options nosniff and a strong ETag (record ETAG, else payload DIGEST, else a weak address+size tag); an If-None-Match match answers 304. The stored bytes are gzipped and the ENCODING IS NEGOTIATED: route reads Accept-Encoding, and a client that refused gzip gets them decoded in-guest and served identity under its OWN strong ETag, because two representations under one tag let a cache holding either answer the other's revalidation with 304. An EMPTY stream is decided by the address's position in the published availability, evaluated the way the CLIENT evaluates it - CesiumTerrainProvider asks computeMaximumLevelAtPosition(centre of the tile) >= level, not per-level membership, so a shallow address over a deep region is one it WILL request: OUTSIDE it a cheap CACHEABLE 404 (public, max-age=300), because a miss below the published pyramid is normal traffic and the client's own upsampling relies on layer.json availability; INSIDE it a SYNTHESIZED height-0 tile (200, public max-age=86400, strong digest ETag, header x-terrain-synthesized), whose water mask is uniform-water only at LEVEL >= the config key terrain_ocean_synth_min_level and uniform-LAND otherwise - fabricated water at a level nothing built paints continents as specular ocean. Any other path is a direct cacheable 404 from route; non-GET/HEAD answers 405. Bridge linkage: the only host crossings are the declared storage.flatsql_query_stream hostcall and plugin.getConfig.

triggers.description: One $HTQ HttpRequest envelope per invocation, pumped by the host at the flow ingress.

api.tagDescription: Quantized-mesh terrain tiles served from this node's $DTT record store (wasm; all routing, conditional-request and response shaping run inside the module). Anonymous by design: every response is cacheable and the record store is read-only from this flow.

routes.summary: Which tileset epoch this node serves
routes.description: The discovery document a client reads to learn WHERE the terrain is, so no client hardcodes a CID or a hostname (owner 2026-08-27: terrain files are requested over IPFS). Names the current tileset CID, its dataset epoch, and terrainBasePath - a path RELATIVE to this node's origin: /ipfs/<cid>/ when a tileset CID is configured ("delivery":"ipfs") and this mount's own prefix when one is not ("delivery":"mount", "cid":null), so a development node with no IPFS daemon answers the same document rather than an error. Keys are lowercase/camelCase: an API-synthesized discovery document, not a $DTT rendered as JSON. cache-control public max-age=60 with a strong ETag - everything under a CID is immutable and this is the lane's ONE mutable pointer, so a minute bounds how long a client can miss a recut while every revalidation after the first is a 304.

application/json.description: Current tileset epoch: tilesetId, delivery, cid, datasetEpoch, terrainBasePath, layerJsonPath, format, scheme, projection, extensions, maxzoom, attribution.

routes.summary: Which tileset epoch this node serves (explicit name)
routes.description: Byte-identical to the mount root, under an explicit filename for clients and caches that prefer a named document to a directory path. Declared as its own route because the host admits a mounted route anonymously only if the flow DECLARES it (sdn-server/internal/gateway/anonymous.go): the delivery path of this whole lane is a client resolving the CID from here, so its anonymity must not rest on an operator allowlist entry alone.

application/json.description: Current tileset epoch: tilesetId, delivery, cid, datasetEpoch, terrainBasePath, layerJsonPath, format, scheme, projection, extensions, maxzoom, attribution.

routes.description: The complete tilejson-2.1.0 descriptor for the served quantized-mesh-1.0 tileset: scheme tms, projection EPSG:4326, bounds [-180,-90,180,90], minzoom 0, configured maxzoom, extensions ["watermask"], and the configured availability index verbatim (octvertexnormals is omitted until normals ship).

The stored quantized-mesh-1.0 tile at TMS address z/x/y (the path's third segment is "<y>.terrain") of the two-root GEOGRAPHIC_WGS84 pyramid (newest stored $DTT record for the address). The body is served VERBATIM from the record's payload: gzip content-encoding as stored, strong ETag, cache-control public max-age=86400. If-None-Match answers 304. An address the tileset never published answers a CACHEABLE 404 (public, max-age=300) - normal traffic, the client upsamples per layer.json availability. An address INSIDE the published availability that the store does not hold is SYNTHESIZED at height 0 rather than 404'd (200, x-terrain-synthesized: uniform-land, or uniform-water only at levels the builder actually built).

params.name: z
params.description: Zoom level, 0 at the pyramid root.

params.name: tile
params.description: Row + extension: "<y>.terrain", TMS row (0 at the south edge).

200.description: The tile bytes, gzip content-encoding, strong ETag.

304.description: Not modified (If-None-Match matched the tile ETag).

404.description: No tile stored at this address (cacheable; clients upsample per layer.json availability).
